subject: Throughput floorplan & data-path latency review for private GPU cluster (Acme Health)
messages:

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com

Subject: Throughput floorplanning for private GPU cluster (Acme Health)

Olga —

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting design work for a VPC-hosted private inference cluster to serve our clinical summarization API. High level requirements: sustained 1200 requests/sec (RPS) at model variant M2 (approx ~2B params) with an average request payload of ~600 tokens, 95th percentile latency target <= 120ms, p99 target <= 250ms. Peak bursts expected to 2.5x sustained for short windows (1–5m).

Constraints that matter on our side:
- Racks are initially provisioned with 4x 100Gb uplinks to leafs (Top-of-Rack switches are Cisco N9K).
- Hosts will be dual-socket, planned to attach to single PCIe fabric; max NIC per host initially 2x100Gb.
- We prefer RDMA for inter-host KV/serving traffic if it's required.
- Procurement lead time for H100-class cards is 10–12 weeks; A40/A10 faster but less throughput.

Attached are sample request profiles and a rough network diagram. Can you outline a floorplan (GPU count and types, per-host NIC guidance, expected RPS per GPU at our token distribution, recommended headroom, and warm-pool strategy)? Also call out any data-path latency floors (switching, kernel bypass, RPC serialization) we should include in SOW/ops SLA.

Thanks,
John
John Edwards
Director, Platform Engineering — Acme Health

Subject: Re: Throughput floorplanning for private GPU cluster (Acme Health)

John —

Appreciate the detail. High-level answer first: we recommend designing to a single latency "floor" composed of (1) model service execution on-GPU, (2) intra-node switch/NIC latency, (3) RPC serialization + TLS, and (4) cache/kV hit/miss delta. For your workload we estimate the cold p95/p99 floor to be dominated by the GPU execution + RPC overhead; with the optimizations below you can hit the 120ms p95 target for sustained load.

Quick proposal (baseline assumptions: M2 ~2B params, quantized INT8 inference, average generation 600 tokens, effective batch size tuned to 8–12):
- Baseline per-GPU throughput (sustained):
  - H100S 80GB (optimized kernels, batch 10, prefix caching): ~350–420 RPS
  - A10G (if used, less memory): ~80–110 RPS (higher variance)
- Floorplanning for 1200 sustained RPS: target capacity = 1200 / 380 ~= 3.2 GPUs -> recommend 4 H100S for baseline.
- Headroom and burst: add 25% practical headroom + warm-pool reserve for KV cache misses -> provision 5 physical GPUs in active pool, maintain 1 additional warm spare per rack for failover (so 6 total in initial order).
- Network/data-path guidance:
  - Use Mellanox/ConnectX-class NICs with SR-IOV and RDMA (GPUDirect when possible) to reduce kernel hops.
  - Enable jumbo frames and set MTU consistently across leaf/spine and hosts.
  - Ensure leaf switch buffer tuning (priority flow control as needed) — aim for <20us transit latency for intra-rack paths.
  - Co-locate KV cache (prefix cache) on the same host where possible to avoid extra hop. If using a shared cache tier, make it RDMA backed to keep extra latency <40ms p99 contribution.
- Autoscaling and operational knobs:
  - Warm pool: keep ~10–15% of baseline concurrent capacity prewarmed (for your profile, 1 GPU warm pool per 6 active GPUs).
  - Scale step: 1 GPU per scale event, cooldown 180s, ramp policy to allow additive batching.
  - Batching policy: allow latency SLO-based batching with hard cap (p95 target) and opportunistic burst batching for p50 improvements.
- Sizing note: if you plan to allow longer sequences (avg tokens >900) re-run the numbers; throughput per GPU drops ~20–30% when average sequence increases from 600 to 900.

I'll attach a compact spreadsheet with the arithmetic. Markus and Rishi — tagging you for confirmation on the per-GPU RPS numbers and any network caveats I'm missing.

Next steps: if that matches expectations, we'll produce a formal SOW with exact SKU counts, lead times, and an ops-runbook for warm-pool maintenance.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Throughput floorplanning for private GPU cluster (Acme Health)

Nice write-up, Olga. A couple conservative adjustments from infra perspective:

1) Per-GPU throughput: our internal bench for M2 @ 600 tokens/req with batching=10 on H100S yields ~320 RPS median and ~290 RPS sustained under realistic RPC contention. Call the planning number 300 RPS/GPU to avoid optimistic underprovisioning.

2) Network headroom: assume 10–15% of link capacity consumed by control & storage traffic; design for 100Gb uplinks but expect effective available ~85Gb for RPCs. Suggest explicitly specifying per-host NIC baseline (2x100Gb LAG) if you want to minimize noisy-neighbor risk.

3) Warm-pool sizes: I've seen warm pools evaporate during cascade restarts; recommend an automated warm-pool reconciliation that ensures at least 2 GPUs worth of warm capacity in cluster across racks (so they survive single rack failure without full cold-start).

4) Procurement lead time & callouts: H100S 80GB lead-time 10–12 weeks; propose a mixed buy: order 3 H100S initially + 3 A10G as interim to hit time-to-market while waiting for H100 shipment. A10s give you ~90 RPS/GPU; use them for non-latency-critical routes.

I'll update Olga's spreadsheet with conservative math and a procurement phasing schedule.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
